text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Serbian government endorses Serbian power industry (EPS) decision not to raise electricity prices but to introduce consumption quotas above which fee will be higher.
- Trepca metal works signs a $4.3 million deal for the export of batteries to Russia, bringing to $65 millon total five-year export of batteries to the country, says director general Novak Bijelic.
- Almost one billion dinars needed to complete Serbia's sowing this year planned to cover 1.07 million hectares, says Serbian cooperative association.
- The negative trade balance with former Yugoslav republics needs to be reduced to a 1:1 parity, says president of the Yugoslav chamber of commerce Mihailo Milojevic.
- September retail price growth at annual low of 1.2 percent in August according to the Federal Statistics Office.
- The main board of the Yugoslav United Left (JUL) accepts proposal of the ruling Socialist party of Serbia (SPS) to join it in a coalition of left-oriented parties at the forthcoming elections.
- Workers of Belgrade motor and tractors industry IMT protest in front of the New Belgrade municipal building demanding outstanding wages and resumption of production.

- Private entrepreneurship ministry plans to ask the Serbian president not to endorse the new law obliging firms to hire two workers. It says the law is turning the clock back to compulsory employment laws and will result in the closure of a large number of firms.
- Price of milk goes up by 25 percent.
- Founder of the Party of Democratic Action (SDA) for Sandzak Sulejman Ugljanin returns to Yugoslavia after a three-year absence to prepare his party for local elections.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic meets U.S. officials to discuss normalisation of bilateral relations with emphasis on strengthening economic cooperation.
- Today new law takes effect reducing income taxes and social security contributions which should save firms some 600 million dinars.
